Bayliss (President), A.R. Shaw. Centre row: C.T. Carter, A.W. Penny, J.A. Kemp, L.J. Cohen. Front row: A.E. Taylor, H.E. Footer. The central figure is, of course, J.C. photos.c: PETER CARTON leads the "Brockman" 800 field at one lap from P. Thomas (7), D. Huffer (11) and J. Sullivan (6). Peter finished 2nd (1:56.3) behind Thomas (1:55.3).

One feature of our Southern League appearances this year has been the faithful band of loyal supporters who have provided the Belgrave team with superb support. Here we see the main ringleaders getting ready for the fray. Yes, your quite right. There's the Couzens, the Pritchards and who's that under the hedge? Quite right it's Bon Viveur and Carshalton Playboy -Ian Richley. But, have you spotted the two Coaches. Yes, the're there-Mick Dunphy and John Sullivan.....So how about a caption for this fine photo -?? The best versions will be printed in the next issue of the BELGRAVIAN.

The officials, pictured left, were (from the top left to right): Gordon Biscoe (timekeeper), John Sullivan (North London timekeeper), Don Anderson (timekeeper), Yak Stegner (Herne Hill timekeeper), Terry Earle (timekeeper), Pat Mead (track referee), Stuart Bennett (track judge), Bob Bridges (timekeeper), Richard Biscoe (track judge), Alan Mead (chief timekeeper), Leslie Earle (track judge). Not pictured but recording entries and assisting with the seeding was John Jeffery while starter was Bob Bush (Serpentine).

photos.c: Belgrave's Winning AAA 12-Stage Team at Sutton Park. Back row: Andy Graffin, Spencer Barden, Paul Freary, Stephen Sharp, Alaster Stewart, David Anderson, Allen Graffin, Paul Evans. Front row: Lee Hurst, Mark Miles, Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward, Charles Herrington.

Above (1): Belgrave's men retained the AAA 6-Stage Road Relay Championship at Sutton Park in October 2002. Mark Miles, Richard Ward, Spencer Barden, Stephen Sharp, Allen Graffin and David Anderson celebrate keeping hold of the trophy for another year. This is the hardest team title to win - can they make it three in a row in October 2003?

Top centre: At the end of his stage Stephen Sharp had clocked the second fastest short stage of the day - second only to our own Andy Graffin - but was later pushed down to third fastest by another Belgravian, David Anderson.
Front page: Stephen Sharp and Martin Dent head the field in the opening "Sweatshop" Surrey CC League Race in Richmond Park.
Right: Stephen Sharp heads a blistering finish in the 1500m at Bedford in the Golden Jubilee Cup Final.
Second left: Yet another Belgravian in the top ten times of the day. Stephen Sharp was fourth best of the day around the short stage and brought the Bels up eight places to second.

Bottom right: The victorious Belgrave crew can't stop smiling after retaining their title. Standing: Jonathan Blackledge (stage 6), Al Stewart (11), Kevin Nash (3), Adam Zawadski (12), Martin Dent (7), Paul Freary (1), Paul Evans (9 - and what proved to be his last team run for Belgrave), David Anderson (4). Kneeling: Allen Graffin (5), Will Cockerell (10), Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward (8), Stephen Sharp (2).
Above: David Anderson, Martin Dent, Will Cockerell, Jonathan Blackledge, Stephen Sharp, Paul Freary - delighted to hold onto the Ian Logan Memorial Bowl for another year.

Above: Stephen Sharp (stage 6), Phil Wicks (2), Jonathan Blackledge (5), Spencer Barden (4), Alaster Stewart (1) and Tim Watson (3) receive the Ian Logan Trophy – Belgrave’s fourth year of being top of the pile at Rushmoor Arena.  Only Stephen and Jonathan remained in the squad from 2004’s winning line-up.
“Sweatshop” Surrey CC League Race 1 at Brockwell Park, and Phil Wicks (9) and Stephen Sharp (1) slug it out at the front of the field.

Above: Maximum points in the 5000 metres.  At the halfway point Mark Miles was closely shadowed by John Nysaginia (Birchfield) and our own Stephen Sharp but by the end of the race the gap was 11 seconds with Stephen heading the B race by 20 seconds.

Peter Gilbey, one of our stalwarts during the cross country season, leads a group during the Senior Mens Surrey C.C.Champs. closely followed by Mark Sinclair and Mick Peel and urged on by a group of Belgrave supporters.

West side story. 1 mile into the 5¾ and the field is bunched waiting for the break. Following Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin are Bob Lettin(71), Leo Coy, Olly Foote, Laurie O'Hara, Mike Nouch,Eric Crutcher(70),Martin Lake,Simon Williamson(68),and Keith Sinclair(22).
ABOVE. Paul Richley hands over to Mark Sinclair in the 25x1 mile relay. Both have shown substantial improvements this year reducing their 1500m times to 3.48.6 and 3.51.8 respectively;

Our victorious team after their outstanding win in the Wellington Relays held on the race course at Ostend.

Front row left to right; Paul Richley, Stuart Paton, Oliver Foote, and Team Manager - Leo Coy.
Mark Sinclair follows Gary Staines in the last British League Match at Battersea Park and in so doing ran a p.b. for the 1500m.

Mark Sinclair has run p.b's in the 1500m, 3000m, 5000m, and 3000s/c this summer. His 1500m time of 3.48.5 is 0.1 faster than John Bicourts p.b. and as John has been advising Mark on hurdling technique it is pleasing to see Mark move to 3rd spot on our all time 3000s/c rankings with a fine 8.56.9. Our strength in this event is considerable with Mike Hayes close to a sub 9.00 effort.

Back Cover.   The South of Thames Junior C.C.Championship provided a unique and exciting spectacle for Belgrave supporters when at the 2 mile mark our men held the first 4 places in the 300 strong field. Our picture shows eventual winner Oliver Foote in the lead from Mark Sinclair(6th), John Gladwin(2nd), and Dave North(7th), the team's winning score being the best ever recorded in the 50 year history of this race - a fitting result with Gordon Biscoe as the S.O.T. President.
BELGRAVE 12 STAGE ROAD RELAY 6.4.86. LEFT.. 1st.TAKEOVER. MARK SINCLAIR TAKES HIS TIME..

Into the bell in the 1500m and they've shed the pacemaker, Stu' Paton (entry fee sponsored by Oliver Foote to set up a sub 4!) Mark Sinclair looks a picture of relaxation and goes on to a sixth successive win. The next three hung on for pb's - Olly, Frank Ward (behind Mark) and John Booth in his seasonal debut after injury!

Gary Staines, fresh from his Olympic 5000m final spearheaded a fine Belgrave team effort in the first Surrey C.C.League Match. Gary (21), Jean Paul Wright (8), followed by Mark Sinclair, Matthew Stickles, Mike Hayes (20), Francis Ward, Marcello Bizio (15) and Ollie Foote (11).

photos.c: For years Derek Clack has said that in all the time he's been in the club he's not yet had his picture published. Sorry Derek - it's a case of too few photographers required to be in too many places at the right time. However, The Wimbledon Guardian seems to be a little better off in the way of human resource and sent their photographer to snap Derek and Sue after their gruelling hike from John O'Groats to Lands End. The 920 mile walk took our intrepid couple seven weeks but it was well worth it for they raised £1000 for the Tadworth Children's Trust. They got lost for a while at Loch Ness and nearly went over a cliff, got stranded out on the West Highland Way as night fell, suffered from blisters ... makes those training reps up Wool Road seem like a piece of cake!

Top (left to right): Phil Spivey watches Racing Club's Yuri Sedykh put the competition beyond anyone else's reach while preparing for his own throw. While eventual 'chase winner Lambruschini lopes along at the back, Justin Chaston is in the thick of the action. Discus thrower Darrin Morris placed 5th. John Regis relaxes in the shade before a scintillating 10.15 100m - as a non-scorer! Spearman Niigel Bevan fires a 3rd-placing 71.78.

Left: It's another win for the Simon family - this time the Girls' 100 metres at Aldershot with Mellisa (BB) crossing the line first. But Mellisa is just one of the "Sporting Simons". Sisters Serrita and Bianca also regularly compete successfully for Belgrave, youngsters Tequila and Max are bit small just yet but add their vocal support, Dad is Peter who trains a boxing team when he is not travelling with the team to urge them on and Mum is Veronica who has putt the shot for us before now.

Proud winner of the 'Centenary Cup' for 1993 was Mellisa Simon, pictured holding the trophy at the Club Dinner after it was presented to her by Olympic and World Championships Hurdler Gowry Retchakan. It was particularly apt that Gowry did the honours because she started off her competitive career in the very same event as that for which Mellisa was awarded the trophy - sprint hurdles.
Not surprisingly the 'Tommy Green Cup' went to John Regis for his silver medal winning run in the World Championships 200 metres where he set new British Record figures of 19.94.

photos.c:
Above: Tremendous discus throwing came from Nick Sweeney throughout the summer of '98 and Helsinborg, Sweden, almost became a second home to the 30 year-old Irishman. Standing 1.95m tall and weighing in at 121kg, Nick previously had a best of 67.40 dating from 1996.

Having travelled to the Swedish town to spin his platter out to 64.28 in July, he was back in August, this time reaching out to 65.59. Not at his best in Budapest for the European Games, Nick barely scraped over 60m but on September 4th, once more in Helsingborg, he launched a mighty 67.89 for his eighth Irish Record - a distance 2 metres in excess of the British Record. Two days later at the same venue he set his second best mark of the season with 65.70.

Nick is a graduate of Harvard University and played Rugby Union for Irish Schools.

photos.c: 1. One of the most glorious sights in athletics is the start of the Senior Men's National Cross Country Championships. Half a mile into the 2000 race at Stowe School, Buckinghhamshire, and the field is led by Belgrave's Paul Evans with Paul Freary just behind him and to the right. On the left, behind 2516 is Kevin Nash and next but one above 2321 is Rob McHarg. On the right, behind the orange vested .24 is Jason Lobo, making a more conservative start, with Lee Hurst next but one on the left of .24. In the centre, just behind and to the right of the Blackheath vest is Alaster Stewart and next on the right, with only his claret bandana showing is Charles Herrington. That's eight in the top 100 and they spent the next half mile gaining even more forward positions. You might have to take the Editor's word for this one: on the skyline just to the left of the tree can be seen Phil Carstairs' thinning thatch. Will Cockerell has also been picked out in this vicinity by one viewer - but blowed if we can find him now!

Right: An hour before "National" race time. Bill Laws and John Jeffery have driven back to Milton Keynes to pick up Paul Evans whose car has broken down, leaving the rest of the team to pose for the pre-race photo. Back row: Eric Hall (President), Don Anderson, Paul Coughlan, Alan Mead, Alaster Stewart, Paul Freary, Jason Lobo, Kevin Nash, Phil Carstairs, Rob Harding. Front: Darryl Ochse, Will Cockerell, Charles Herrington, Lee Hurst, Rob McHarg.

Above: Irish eyes were not the only ones smiling when the the Belgrave team collected their prizes in Wallace Park. Rob McHarg, Paul Freary, Alaster Stewart, Yacin Yusuf (crouching), Jason Lobo and Spencer Barden enjoy being Irish Road Relay Champions.

Belgrave's Winning AAA 12-Stage Team at Sutton Park. Back row: Andy Graffin, Spencer Barden, Paul Freary, Stephen Sharp, Alaster Stewart, David Anderson, Allen Graffin, Paul Evans. Front row: Lee Hurst, Mark Miles, Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward, Charles Herrington.

Third from left: Alaster Stewart took leg 11 and ran a personal best for the long stage; the Belgrave lead went up to over 2 minutes. Sadly, Al became injured some time after this high and has yet to make a return to training.

Bottom right: The victorious Belgrave crew can't stop smiling after retaining their title. Standing: Jonathan Blackledge (stage 6), Al Stewart (11), Kevin Nash (3), Adam Zawadski (12), Martin Dent (7), Paul Freary (1), Paul Evans (9 - and what proved to be his last team run for Belgrave), David Anderson (4). Kneeling: Allen Graffin (5), Will Cockerell (10), Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward (8), Stephen Sharp (2).

Above: Stephen Sharp (stage 6), Phil Wicks (2), Jonathan Blackledge (5), Spencer Barden (4), Alaster Stewart (1) and Tim Watson (3) receive the Ian Logan Trophy – Belgrave’s fourth year of being top of the pile at Rushmoor Arena.  Only Stephen and Jonathan remained in the squad from 2004’s winning line-up.
